phases.name: Phase 1 · Leaving Notion
phases.blurb: Everything moves into plain files on your own machine, and the first ways in: capture, mail, chat and fitness.

phases.name: Phase 2 · The server takes over
phases.blurb: Jobs run on the server with nobody watching, and the system starts checking itself.

phases.name: Phase 3 · Talking to it
phases.blurb: You message the vault from your phone, and it starts messaging you back.

phases.name: Phase 4 · Running the day
phases.blurb: From storing things to planning them: mornings, weeks, trips and every inbox.

phases.name: Phase 5 · Sharing it
phases.blurb: Public, and updating itself. The current phase: new changes land here as they ship.

entries.title: Carmen goes online
entries.summary: The kit gets a public home: an always-current download, the Start Here guide and this history. Every night the code is copied, stripped of anything personal, checked by two privacy scanners and only then published.

entries.title: LinkedIn, Messenger, Instagram
entries.summary: Messages from all three reach Claude, read-only, with a push when someone new writes.

entries.title: Meeting recordings
entries.summary: Recorded meetings and talks are pulled from Wispr Flow and filed next to the project they belong to, readable with the laptop off.

entries.title: Travel
entries.summary: Door-to-door search across every nearby airport, trains and ferries, with bags included in every price, and fare watches that push you when a price drops.

entries.title: Realistic weeks
entries.summary: How long recurring things really take, door to door, and the rules for placing work into a day, so a week plan says plainly when it does not fit.

entries.title: Listen to your readings
entries.summary: Documents go to Speechify in one request, to listen to on a walk or a commute.

entries.title: Tasks that stay well-formed
entries.summary: A checker runs after every edit, so every task keeps a clear next step, whoever wrote it.

entries.title: When is the group free?
entries.summary: Ask when most of a group chat can do dinner, and Claude compares everyone's calendars in one request.

entries.title: The morning check-in
entries.summary: Overnight the server reads mail, chats and the calendar and guesses where every task stands. After the morning journal you confirm with one click per task, and today goes into the calendar.

entries.title: Sessions that remember
entries.summary: A rolling log of what every Claude session worked on, so the next one picks up where the last stopped.

entries.title: The kit
entries.summary: The whole setup packaged for friends: a Start Here guide, a walkthrough, a vault template and the code, set up by Claude one approved step at a time.

entries.title: Telegram, and the vault speaks first
entries.summary: The vault becomes a Telegram bot: voice notes, files, one thread per topic, and Allow / Deny buttons before anything goes out. For the first time the server messages you, starting with the weekly brief.

entries.title: One Monday brief
entries.summary: Everything that needs you from the maintenance side arrives as one note on Monday, instead of a stream of mail.

entries.title: Readings on the Kindle
entries.summary: Course readings, cases and articles go to the Kindle in one request.

entries.title: Build backlog
entries.summary: Ideas tagged during the week become one plan on Monday, with each item scoped by its own Claude session.

entries.title: People
entries.summary: One note per person, with circles from inner to dormant, open loops as fields and nine views. Contacts, class lists and chats can be imported into it.

entries.title: Routine reminders
entries.summary: Morning and evening routine pushes to the phone, with the text kept in the vault so changing a routine means editing a note.

entries.title: Alerts you actually see
entries.summary: Urgent things go out as a push to the phone, and only what can wait goes to email.

entries.title: WhatsApp bridge
entries.summary: Message your vault on WhatsApp and Claude answers, files and acts on it, with alerts if the connection drops.

entries.title: It tests itself
entries.summary: The server runs its own test suite on a timer and catches jobs that run but were never committed, and tasks sitting where no view can see them.

entries.title: A morning journal
entries.summary: A meditation and journal note is created every morning. It later becomes the start of the morning check-in.

entries.title: Learnings, consolidated
entries.summary: Insights captured during the week are distilled into one running notebook, in the language they were written in.

entries.title: Backups and a map
entries.summary: Encrypted nightly backups to Backblaze B2 with restore tests, and a map of every folder that is rewritten from disk each week.

entries.title: Your own wiki
entries.summary: Claude distils your sources into topic articles, so a question about what you know or think is answered from your own material first.

entries.title: Transcription
entries.summary: Lectures, podcasts and videos are transcribed offline in about 99 languages, straight into the notes.

entries.title: Course archive
entries.summary: Every Canvas course, page, file and assignment archived into the vault with the text extracted, so Claude can say what a class covered and which readings are due.

entries.title: Jobs with a watchdog
entries.summary: One shared runner for every scheduled job, a heartbeat that watches the others, and a weekly all-green digest. The code gets its own history from here on.

entries.title: Profiles with a shelf life
entries.summary: Facts about you live in one Master Profile with sub-profiles, each fact dated so stale ones get questioned rather than trusted. A registry of property names stops two systems claiming the same one.

entries.title: Working conditions
entries.summary: A note of when work can realistically happen, so plans respect energy, classes and commitments instead of assuming an empty week.

entries.title: Nothing goes stale silently
entries.summary: A registry of everything that can quietly stop being true, from login tokens to documents, each with how it gets checked.

entries.title: Fitness data
entries.summary: Strava and WHOOP sync to the server, so training and recovery sit next to everything else.

entries.title: Both mailboxes
entries.summary: Personal and school Gmail, readable and draftable by Claude from one place.

entries.title: Capture in two seconds
entries.summary: The iPhone Action Button and a Mac hotkey drop any thought into the Inbox.

entries.title: A task cockpit and a daily loop
entries.summary: Tasks become notes with a status, priority and next step, reviewed in one Obsidian layout. Dump, commit, prioritise, schedule becomes the rhythm.

entries.title: Chats as a source
entries.summary: WhatsApp becomes material Claude can read, so plans and promises made in messages stop getting lost.

entries.title: An always-on server
entries.summary: A small Linux server keeps a synced copy of the vault and runs Claude Code around the clock, reachable only over a private network.

entries.title: From Notion to plain files
entries.summary: Notes, tasks and plans move out of Notion into an Obsidian vault of Markdown files, so an AI agent can search thousands of them locally in milliseconds instead of one API call per page.
